content:
The BrownianMotion project is currently incompatible with Mathlib, in the sense that if you create a lean file there and write

import Mathlib
import BrownianMotion

you get an error because we have a duplicated declaration. This is not seen in our CI because the Mathlib file with the declaration is not imported by the BrownianMotion files. But someone wanted to use both repositories and ran into the issue. Fixing the problem will be simple but I'd like to make sure that the issue does not happen again.

We could detect it by having such an "import everything" file in the project, but that would greatly increase our CI times. Is there a more lightweight way to check that?
I think flt has such a file. Why would it greatly increase build times?

I think the docgen step is the one that will take much longer, not the build? I'm remembering seeing that increased CI time effect in other blueprint projects when I merged an import Mathlib by mistake.
But I'll try the import everything file approach and see if the effect I'm remembering is real.

My proposed solution in FLT doesn't work as it stands: https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/FLT/pull/778 . I'm just merging main to remind me of what the problem was (the logs have expired).

I would love to see this working because the same thing happened to us too. I am hoping that my proposed solution will not put us in the doc-gen hell which Remy is outlining. I agree that any file which accidentally imports Mathlib suddenly makes doc-gen (and thus CI) take over an hour (I think the check is here https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/FLT/blob/a48ce3fb032d09c88f828374e2f942d980431c22/.github/workflows/blueprint.yml#L50-L53 ). We also have CI stopping us from importing Mathlib (and this is great because import Mathlib is very useful for prototyping but I often forget to remove it)

Could you make an auxiliary lean file whose sole content is

import Mathlib
import BrownianMotion

and run lake build Aux.lean in CI?

It seems to work, actually:

  error: FLTTest/MathlibCompatibility.lean:6:0: import FLT.Deformations.Subfunctor failed, environment already contains 'CategoryTheory.Subfunctor.ctorIdx' from Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Subfunctor.Basic
Isnt that similar to the approach mathlib takes, i.e. make such a file a test file?
I'm not sure what the question is? The PR to FLT adds this auxiliary lean file to a test library, for which no documentation is generated

Thanks for the pointers. I tried to adapt the FLT PR to the BrownianMotion project, but checkdecls is not happy with that setup: https://github.com/RemyDegenne/brownian-motion/pull/392
Anyone knows what I could do about it?
Oh, that's annoying. It looks like FLT didn't actually get to that point because it caught an error earlier, so I may have been too optimistic
However, maybe it would work if you added a step in your workflow to build the new library before the docgen-action step
